body_md: For all $\ell ,r\in \mathbb{N}$ with $\ell \geq 3$ or $r\geq 3$ there exist oriented graphs $D_1$ and $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1) =\ell$ and $\operatorname{inv}(D_2) =r$, but $\operatorname{inv}(D_1\rightarrow D_2)< \operatorname{inv}(D_1) + \operatorname{inv}(D_2)$.

label: thm:all_ell_r
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:all_ell_r}
    There exists $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $\ell ,r\in \mathbb{N}$ with $\ell,r \geq k$, there exist tournaments $D_1$ and $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1) =\ell$ and $\operatorname{inv}(D_2) =r$, but $\operatorname{inv}(D_1\rightarrow D_2)< \operatorname{inv}(D_1) + \operatorname{inv}(D_2)$.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $D$ be a tournament with $V(D)=(v_1,v_2,\dots,v_n)$. We say that an $n\times n$ symmetric matrix $M$ with entries in $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a \emph{decycling matrix} for $D$, if reversing the orientation of all arcs $v_iv_j$ where $m_{ij}=1$, results in a tournament with no directed cycles.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: Let $D$ be a tournament. The \emph{tournament minimum rank} of $D$, denoted $\operatorname{tmr}(D)$, is the smallest rank of a decycling matrix for $D$.

title: Proof
body_md: If $\operatorname{tmr}(D) \leq k$, then there exists a decycling matrix $M$ for $D$ of rank at most $k$. Reversing the arcs of $D$ according to $M$ gives a corresponding  linear order $<$ on the vertices of $D$. The tournament $D$ is recovered from $(<,M)$ by reversing the arcs of the transitive tournament according to $M$. Thus the set of tournaments with $\operatorname{tmr} \leq k$ can be indexed by the set of pairs $(<,M)$ of linear orders and symmetric matrices of rank $ \leq k$. There are $n!$ orders and $\sum_{j \leq k} N(n,j)$ such matrices. The result now follows directly from Lemma \ref{lem:Mc1} with $q = 2$.
